jobs.title: Technical GTM Strategy & Operations Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT CAMPFIRE

Campfire is an AI-native ERP designed for mid-size and enterprise companies to streamline operations and accelerate growth. With features like a powerful general ledger, AI-powered agents and actions, and seamless integrations with industry-leading solutions, Campfire caters to a diverse range of businesses, from tech companies to non-profits.

Headquartered in San Francisco, Campfire is a Y Combinator company that has raised over $100M across its Series A and Series B rounds, led by Accel and Ribbit Capital.

THE ROLE

As our Technical GTM Strategy & Operations Lead, you will build the infrastructure and insight to support our technical GTM members. This is the connective role between our SCs, Sales, and Product. You will be part operator, part builder, and part analyst. You'll own the systems and processes that get our prospects into the our pilot programs faster, measure the data that tells us what's working, and the enablement that keeps the entire GTM org sharp on a product that ships every week.

If you like turning a high-performing but scrappy team into a well-instrumented machine, building the tooling, tracking the numbers, and running the pilots that shorten sales cycles, this is a role with enormous surface area and direct impact on our growth trajectory.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design and automate our customer pilots and sandboxes: building the baseline environments SCs personalize for each prospect, and the tooling that makes spin-up, reset, and teardown fast and repeatable.

 - Instrument and track pilot usage: who's touching the product, which modules, how often, and turn that into a clear picture of pilot health and prospect engagement.

 - Own demo/pilot → POC → close conversion analytics, tying product-touch data to deal outcomes so we understand what actually moves good-fit deals forward.

 - Build and track SC performance analytics, giving the team and leadership a shared, honest view of what's working and where to invest.

 - Own the operations of our SC demo-request routing: configuration, round-robin and ramp-weighting logic, and the admin relationships that keep it running, so demos land with the right SC every time.

 - Build internal tooling and automation for the SC workflow itself: provisioning scripts, agent templates, and the handoff assets that make SCs faster.

 - Lead pilot enablement and feature enablement for the wider GTM org: training SCs, AEs, and SDRs on new product areas so the whole team can sell the value we're building as it ships.

 - Stand up competitive and field-signal instrumentation: standardizing how prospect feedback and competitive intel get captured during pilots and routed back to Product as structured, actionable signal.

QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience in a GTM operations, sales engineering, solutions/revenue operations, or technical enablement role, ideally in a fast-moving B2B SaaS environment.

 - A strong background in accounting and finance related topics to develop a core understanding of production functionality.

 - Technical builder's instinct: comfortable writing scripts, wiring up automation and integrations (APIs, internal tooling, AI agents), and standing up systems from scratch rather than waiting for them.

 - Strong analytical skills, with the ability to define the right metrics, build the tracking, and turn usage and pipeline data into decisions.

 - Familiarity with the GTM stack (CRM such as HubSpot, calendar/workspace admin, sandbox/demo environments) and a knack for making tools talk to each other.

 - Excellent communicator who can train and enable others, from SCs to AEs to SDRs.

 - Entrepreneurial mindset with a desire to help build something from the ground up.

 - Self-motivated and comfortable working in a fast-paced startup environment.

WHY CAMPFIRE

 - Competitive compensation including meaningful equity.

 - Opportunity to shape a product that is transforming how businesses manage their accounting.

 - Work directly with the founding team and have significant impact on company direction.

 - Build the backbone of a GTM org at a hyper-growth, AI-native company, with the autonomy to define the role as you go.

jobs.title: Senior Partner Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
About Campfire
Campfire is a next-gen core accounting platform built for modern mid-market finance teams. We’re building the future of ERP by replacing outdated systems and manual accounting processes with an AI-native platform that helps finance teams move faster and operate more efficiently.

About the role

Partners extend Campfire's reach into accounts and communities we can't get to alone. You'll build the partner marketing function from the ground up: joint value propositions and co-marketing programs with our most important partners, partner-sourced pipeline programs, and the enablement that helps partners sell and market Campfire well.

What you'll do

 - Build the partner marketing plan with the Partnerships team: partner tiering, program design, budget and pipeline targets.

 - Develop joint messaging and “better together” assets with priority partners: solution briefs, integration pages, webinars and joint customer stories.

 - Run co-marketing campaigns and joint events with partners alongside Field Marketing and Corporate Events, including marketplace and directory presence.

 - Own partner-facing enablement: portal content, launch communications, sales playbooks and a partner newsletter.

 - Manage market development funds and co-funded programs where they apply, and track their return.

 - Own Campfire's presence at partner conferences and communities, coordinating sponsorships with Field Marketing.

 - Report on partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and on partner engagement.

What you'll bring

 - 8+ years in B2B marketing, including 3+ in partner, channel or ecosystem marketing at a software company.

 - A track record of building partner co-marketing programs that produced measurable pipeline.

 - Experience with both technology or integration partners and services partners, plus familiarity with marketplaces and partner portals.

 - Strong relationship skills; you align internal and external stakeholders with different incentives.

 - Excellent writing; you can turn a partnership into a clear, differentiated joint story.

 - Comfort with events, webinars and campaign execution. You're a builder who ships.

jobs.title: Customer Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
About Campfire
Campfire is a next-gen core accounting platform built for modern mid-market finance teams. We’re building the future of ERP by replacing outdated systems and manual accounting processes with an AI-native platform that helps finance teams move faster and operate more efficiently.

About the role

Customer proof is Campfire's most persuasive marketing, and you'll own all of it. You'll build the customer marketing engine from the ground up, which includes a steady flow of case studies and proof points, a reference and advocacy program sales can lean on, a review-site strategy, and management of our customer community including our customer advisory board. Every team in Marketing and Sales will come to you, so you'll prioritize ruthlessly and communicate clearly.

What you'll do

 - Build and run the case-study and proof-point program: source candidates with Customer Success and Sales, run interviews, write and produce stories in multiple formats, and maintain a searchable proof library with quantified outcomes.

 - Own the customer reference program: recruit, tier and manage advocates; run the reference request process for Sales; track usage and protect customers from being over-asked.

 - Build and run the advocacy and community program: manage Campfire's customer Slack community day-to-day and run an in-person community program (meetups, dinners, advisory boards), alongside speaking opportunities, peer-to-peer events, and recognition that keeps advocates engaged.

 - Nominate and submit customers for industry awards and recognition programs, and manage the submission process end to end.

 - Own review-site strategy and execution on G2, Capterra and peers: review generation campaigns, profile management, badges and report placement, and using review data in sales and marketing.

 - Produce customer video and testimonials with the Content / Storytelling team, from short social clips to full stories captured at events.

 - Supply proof points for launches and campaigns to Product Marketing, Growth, Brand and Field; support customer speakers at Corporate Events.

 - Measure impact: reference wins influenced, review volume and rating, proof coverage by segment and use case, advocate satisfaction.

What you'll bring

 - 4+years in B2B marketing, with direct ownership of a reference, case-study, or similar customer-facing program.

 - Excellent interviewing and writing; you draw out specifics and quantify results.

 - Experience running review-site programs on G2 or Capterra and an understanding of how buyers use them.

 - Empathy for customers and a service mindset toward Sales and Customer Success; you protect relationships while still hitting targets.

 - Strong project and stakeholder management across many parallel requests.

 - Comfort producing video (briefing, on-camera interviews, working with editors) even if you don't edit yourself.



Must have

 - Experience with advocacy and reference platforms (UserEvidence, Influitive, ReferenceEdge or similar) and G2 Buyer Intent.

 - Experience building a program from zero at a scaling company.

 - Event experience: customer speaker coordination and on-site capture.

 - Comfortable hosting and presenting to CFOs and senior finance leaders, including running our customer advisory board.

jobs.title: Senior Content Marketing Manager, Storytelling
jobs.description:
About Campfire
Campfire is a next-gen core accounting platform built for modern mid-market finance teams. We’re building the future of ERP by replacing outdated systems and manual accounting processes with an AI-native platform that helps finance teams move faster and operate more efficiently.

About the role

You'll be Campfire's lead storyteller: the person who finds the narratives in our customers, our product and our point of view on the market, and turns them into content people want to read, watch and share. You'll set the editorial agenda for brand content, write and edit across formats, and work side by side with our video producer, social lead, product marketers and customer marketer to give Campfire a distinctive, consistent voice.

What you'll do

 - Own the brand editorial strategy and calendar: narratives, series and formats across long-form, newsletter, video scripts and social.

 - Write and edit thought leadership, customer stories (with Customer Marketing), founder and executive content, launch narratives, and scripts and show formats for video.

 - Define and steward Campfire's voice: build the style guide and coach contributors across Marketing.

 - Develop original, source-worthy content (research, data stories, frameworks) that earns attention and strengthens SEO and AEO authority.

 - Co-plan with the SEO & AEO Manager to align topics and avoid duplication; hand off or co-produce where intents overlap.

 - Partner with Social and Influencer Marketing on distribution and with Creative on visual storytelling.

 - Measure what resonates (engagement, subscribers, assisted pipeline, qualitative feedback) and evolve the program.

What you'll bring

 - 6+ years in content marketing, journalism or editorial, with a portfolio that shows range and a recognizable voice.

 - Exceptional writing and editing; you make complex B2B topics clear and interesting.

 - Experience building an editorial program (a newsletter, series or brand publication) from concept to audience.

 - Comfort scripting for video and collaborating with producers.

 - A collaborative operating style: you work across SEO, Product Marketing, Social and Customer Marketing without turf wars.

 - Sound judgment on brand, tone and what's worth saying.

Nice to have

 - Experience in [Campfire's category] or with the personas we sell to.

 - Newsletter growth experience.

 - Basic SEO literacy.

What success looks like in 90 days

 - Editorial strategy, voice guide and Q1 calendar published.

 - One flagship series (written or video) and the newsletter cadence launched.

 - Content boundaries and a joint calendar agreed with SEO & AEO.

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
As a Customer Success Manager at Campfire, you will own a portfolio of customers and be responsible for driving adoption, retention, and long-term success. You will be the primary partner to finance and accounting teams, ensuring customers realize measurable value from Campfire and feel confident running their core financial operations on our platform.

You will work closely with Implementation, Product, Support, and Sales to deliver a best-in-class customer experience and identify opportunities for expansion and growth.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


CUSTOMER OWNERSHIP & SUCCESS

 - Own post-implementation success for a portfolio of customers
   

 - Build strong relationships with Controllers, Accounting Managers, and Finance leaders
   

 - Drive adoption, engagement, and value realization across accounts
   

 - Proactively manage account health and identify churn risk
   

 - Lead QBRs, success planning, and ongoing check-ins
   


RETENTION & GROWTH

 - Manage renewals for your book of business
   

 - Identify and support expansion opportunities (seats, modules, entities, geographies, use cases)
   

 - Partner with Sales to scope and close upsell and cross-sell opportunities
   

 - Maintain accurate renewal forecasts and risk pipelines
   


PRODUCT ADOPTION & ENABLEMENT

 - Lead customer enablement sessions and workflow optimization reviews
   

 - Support rollout of new product features and modules
   

 - Ensure customers are following best practices and getting maximum value from Campfire
   


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION

 - Partner closely with Implementation to ensure smooth handoffs and successful go-lives
   

 - Work with Support and Product to resolve issues and escalate customer feedback
   

 - Represent customer voice internally and help improve processes across the customer lifecycle
   


EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years of Customer Success or Account Management experience in B2B SaaS
   

 - Experience supporting finance, accounting, or operations teams strongly preferred
   

 - Bonus: ERP or accounting software experience (QuickBooks, Xero, Sage Intacct, NetSuite)
   

 - Strong technical aptitude and ability to learn complex platforms quickly
   

 - Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience
   


PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES

 - Customer-first mindset with strong ownership and accountability
   

 - Excellent communicator and relationship builder
   

 - Organized, proactive, and comfortable managing multiple accounts
   

 - Strong problem-solver who thrives in a fast-moving startup environment
   

 - Growth mindset and eagerness to learn and develop

jobs.title: Sales Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT CAMPFIRE

Campfire is the AI-native ERP redefining how finance teams operate. We replace legacy systems like NetSuite, SAP, and Oracle with a unified platform for the general ledger, revenue automation, and close management - powered by our proprietary Large Accounting Model. We're backed by Accel, Ribbit Capital, Foundation Capital, and Y Combinator, and trusted by fast-growing companies like Decagon, Replit, and Klarity. With more than $100m in funding so far, we're scaling the team that closes and expands relationships with modern finance leaders.



THE ROLE

We're hiring a Sales Manager to lead a team of Account Executives - the people who take a qualified opportunity and turn it into a closed, thriving Campfire customer. You'll own quota attainment for your team, coach AEs through complex, consultative sales cycles into finance and accounting orgs, and instill the rigor and discipline of a high-performing sales floor. This is a player-coach leadership role for someone who loves the deal, knows how to develop closers, and wants to help build a repeatable, scalable sales motion from an early foundation.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead, coach, and develop a team of Account Executives to consistently meet and exceed revenue targets.

 - Own your team's number: forecast accurately, manage the pipeline, and drive quota attainment quarter over quarter.

 - Coach AEs through full-cycle, consultative deals - discovery, business-case building, multithreading, negotiation, and close - selling to CFOs, VPs of Finance, and Controllers.

 - Run disciplined deal reviews and pipeline inspection, help reps navigate complex, multi-stakeholder evaluations that often displace incumbent ERPs.

 - Refine and document the sales playbook: qualification frameworks (e.g., MEDDPICC), messaging, and repeatable close plans.

 - Partner with SDR Managers on pipeline quality and handoffs, and with Marketing, Product, and Solutions Consultants on what's needed to win.

 - Hire and onboard new AEs, and build a ramp program that gets them productive quickly.

 - Build the team from the ground up - source, interview, and hire AEs, and design a ramp program that gets new reps productive quickly

 - Maintain clean forecasting and CRM hygiene, and report on team performance to leadership.

 - Foster a culture of accountability, coaching, and winning - where reps are challenged and supported in equal measure.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 2+ years managing a quota-carrying AE team, with a consistent record of hitting and exceeding team targets.

 - A strong personal track record closing B2B SaaS deals before you moved into management - ideally mid-market or enterprise.

 - Track record of holding Account Executives accountable for self-sourced outbound prospecting in a full-cycle sales motion - not just managing our inbound-heavy pipeline.

 - Experience selling technical or finance-oriented products; familiarity with the office of the CFO, ERP, fintech, or accounting workflows is a big plus.

 - Command of a modern sales methodology (MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, Challenger, or similar) and the ability to teach it.

 - Sharp forecasting instincts and comfort running data-driven pipeline reviews.

 - A genuine coaching orientation - you measure your success by your team's growth and results.

 - Thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where the playbook is still being written.


WHY CAMPFIRE

 - Own revenue outcomes at a Series B company in a category that's being rebuilt for the AI era.

 - Shape the sales motion and culture that will scale Campfire to its next stage.

 - Competitive salary and OTE, meaningful equity, and full benefits.

 - Work alongside exceptional operators and sell a product that's replacing software finance teams have been golden handcuffed by for decades.

jobs.title: Field Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
Field Marketing Manager · New York City · Full-time, in-market


THE ROLE

New York is where many of our highest-value buyers already are. We are hiring a Field Marketing Manager to turn that density into a pipeline — through tradeshows, community programs, hackathons, executive dinners, and hospitality experiences that people actually remember.

This is an owner's role, not a coordinator's. You will decide which shows are worth attending, which communities are worth investing in, who belongs at which dinner table, and where the next dollar goes. You will work shoulder to shoulder with Sales, and you will be measured on the pipeline your programs create and accelerate.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Own the NYC event portfolio — strategy, budget, execution, and reporting across a range of program types

 - Tradeshows: select and tier shows against our target accounts, design the booth experience, and hold the team to pre-show outreach and post-show follow-up.

 - Communities: build a sustained presence with NYC practitioner communities and peer networks — recurring formats, real partnerships, and customer advocates on stage.

 - Hackathons: partner with Product and Engineering to run events that earn technical credibility and get builders using the product.

 - Executive dinners: curate small, high-signal rooms of senior buyers, built account by account with Sales, with follow-up that converts.

 - Hospitality: design sports, culture, and dining experiences tied to named deals, with clear allocation rules and compliance guardrails.

 - Build and negotiate budgets across vendors, venues, sponsorships, software, and agencies — and defend the ROI.

 - Report honestly on what worked and what did not, and present plans and results to the wider GTM team.

 - Leave a process behind — playbooks, templates, and SLAs so every program is repeatable and scalable to the next market.


WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - 4–7 years in field marketing, events, or experiential marketing, including B2B with a sales-led motion.

 - A track record of running events independently, end to end, with minimal oversight.

 - Range across event types — you have done the big show and the eight-person dinner, and you know they are different jobs.

 - Strong Sales partnership skill: you can build an invite list account by account, push back on low-leverage asks, and chase follow-up.

 - Data fluency: you build plans from account and performance data and can talk about cost per meeting without flinching.

 - Strong negotiation instincts with vendors, venues, and agencies.

 - Excellent presence in front of a room, including senior internal audiences.

 - Based in NYC, with willingness to work evenings and travel to EMEA 
   
   Nice to have

 - Experience with technical or developer audiences (hackathons, builder communities).

 - Existing NYC venue, agency, and community relationships.

 - Experience selling to or marketing to finance and accounting leaders.

 - Experience mentoring junior marketers or managing agency teams.


HOW WE WILL KNOW IT IS WORKING

Within a year, the NYC portfolio has a defensible cost per qualified meeting, a repeatable playbook for each program type, and pipeline contribution that the sales team would happily defend in a QBR.

jobs.title: Tech Partnerships Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT CAMPFIRE

Campfire is an AI-native ERP built for mid-sized and enterprise companies. We help finance and accounting teams replace spreadsheets, manual reconciliations, and disconnected systems with one modern platform.

We’re backed by Y Combinator and have offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. We’ve raised more than $100 million, including a $35 million Series A led by Accel.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Campfire works best when it connects seamlessly with the rest of a company’s technology and finance stack. That’s where you come in.

We’re looking for a Tech Partnerships Lead to build strong relationships with the software companies our customers already use—from banking, payroll, and spend management platforms to CRM, FP&A, and revenue tools.

You’ll own these partnerships from beginning to end: identifying the right companies, building relationships, negotiating agreements, launching integrations, and creating opportunities for both companies to generate revenue together.

This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to build. You’ll help shape our partnership strategy, decide where we should invest, and turn our strongest technology partnerships into a meaningful source of customers and revenue.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and manage relationships with Campfire’s technology partners.

 - Identify the partners that matter most to our customers and business, and focus our time accordingly.

 - Find and develop new partnership opportunities.

 - Lead partnership conversations from the initial introduction through negotiation, agreement, and launch.

 - Work with Sales and our partners to share leads, collaborate on opportunities, and close business together.

 - Partner with Product and Engineering to decide which integrations we should build and what each one needs to deliver.

 - Coordinate launches and marketing programs with partners, including webinars, content, events, and marketplace listings.

 - Give Campfire’s sales team and our partners the training, materials, and messaging they need to explain the partnership to customers.

 - Track the leads, pipeline, customers, and revenue generated through partnerships.

 - Regularly share what’s working, what isn’t, and where we should invest next.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Significant experience building technology partnerships, business development relationships, or strategic alliances.

 - Experience working directly with software or integration partners.

 - A track record of building partnerships that generated customers, pipeline, or revenue.

 - Confidence negotiating commercial agreements, referral terms, revenue-sharing arrangements, and joint commitments.

 - A strong understanding of business and finance software. You should be familiar with categories such as ERP, banking, payroll, spend management, and financial planning.

 - Enough technical knowledge to discuss APIs, data, and integrations with product and engineering teams—and explain those concepts clearly to nontechnical audiences.

 - Strong commercial judgment and an ability to prioritize the opportunities that can create the most value.

 - Clear, persuasive written and verbal communication.

 - Comfort working in a fast-moving environment where the program and playbook are still being built.

 - Willingness to work from our San Francisco or New York office and travel occasionally for partner meetings and events.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience at a fast-growing B2B software company, especially in fintech, accounting, or ERP.

 - Experience building a technology partnership program at an early-stage company.

 - Familiarity with tools such as Crossbeam, HubSpot, or a partner relationship management platform.

 - Experience managing people, or an interest in building and leading a team as the program grows.


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

 - Meaningful equity

 - Medical, dental, and vision coverage

 - 401(k)

 - $10,000 in family-building benefits through Carrot, plus parental leave

 - Daily catered meals in our San Francisco, New York, and London offices

 - Commuter benefits and regular team events

Final compensation will depend on experience, location, and interview performance.


OUR INTERVIEW PROCESS

 1. Initial chat with the Recruiting team

 2. Introductory conversation with the Head of Tech Partnerships

 3. A working session about Campfire’s technology ecosystem and where you would focus first- Case Study

 4. Onsite : Conversations with people from Sales, Product, and Marketing & Final conversation with company leadership

Campfire is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We provide reasonable accommodations throughout the hiring process.

jobs.title: VC Partnerships Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT CAMPFIRE

Campfire is an AI-native ERP built for mid-sized and enterprise companies. We help finance and accounting teams replace spreadsheets, manual reconciliations, and disconnected systems with one modern platform.

We’re backed by Y Combinator and have offices in San Francisco, New York, and London. We’ve raised more than $100 million, including a $35 million Series A led by Accel.

About the Role

We're looking for a strategic, well-connected partnerships leader to build our venture capital partnerships function from the ground up. You'll design and run a scalable program that engages venture firms, VC-backed companies, and the broader startup ecosystem. You'll work closely with our Head of PE & VC Practice, who will support you as you build the function.

The ideal candidate has already built a VC partnerships role or program from scratch, ideally at a technology startup. Experience selling or partnering around Office of the CFO technology is a strong plus.

What You'll Do

 - Design, launch, and own our VC partnerships strategy.

 - Build senior relationships with venture capital firms, accelerators, and other startup ecosystem partners.

 - Create partnership programs that deliver value to both sides, including customer introductions, portfolio company engagement, co-marketing, thought leadership, and strategic intelligence.

 - Serve as the main point of contact for VC partners, with a clear and consistent story for why they should work with us.

 - Work closely with Sales, Marketing, Product, Customer Success, Strategy, and Executive Leadership to turn partnership activity into pipeline, revenue, adoption, and brand impact.

 - Build repeatable ways to source and manage opportunities from VC partners, including referral processes, partner enablement, reporting, and feedback loops.

 - Develop executive relationship plans for priority firms, and bring in senior leadership where it will strengthen the partnership.

 - Host and run our own VC events, and represent the company at industry events, investor meetings, portfolio company forums, and ecosystem gatherings.

 - Track market trends, investment activity, and emerging companies to spot strategic opportunities and inform internal decisions.

What You'll Bring

 - 3–7 years of experience in partnerships, business development, venture capital, startup ecosystems, strategic alliances, or a related commercial role.

 - Proven experience taking a VC partnerships role, function, or program from zero to a repeatable operating model.

 - Established relationships and credibility with VC firms, investors, founders, and startup ecosystem leaders.

 - A track record of partnerships that delivered measurable business results.

 - Strong executive presence and the ability to earn trust with senior external partners and internal stakeholders.
